title: JPMorgan doesn't expect AI stocks to rebound like July
source_used: MarketWatch (text read via Longbridge; the Quartz page was blocked)
key_facts: JPMorgan's global strategy team does not expect October's AI sell-off to recover as fast as July's did.
Strategist Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou cites weaker buy-the-dip sentiment, dwindled company buybacks, fewer short positions and more leveraged ETF assets.
AI infrastructure stocks 'do not appear oversold from a positioning or flow perspective'.
SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics have fallen almost a third in the last month.
The two firms announced buybacks totalling $40 billion that finished earlier than expected in mid-October; July had no such buyback cliff.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ETF SOX dropped 10% in five sessions.
quote_evidence: July was an ugly month for artificial-intelligence stocks but the correction was short-lived and the rebound fast and meaningful.
The worrying implication for investors who own AI infrastructure stocks then, is that, despite this current selloff, they "do not appear oversold from a positioning or flow perspective."
why_it_matters_hint: JPMorgan sees fewer supports for a quick rebound than in July.
